To create (a hole) by removing material with a drill (tool).

examples.text: Drill a small hole to start the screw in the right direction.

glosses: To practice, especially in (or as in) a military context.

examples.text: They drilled daily to learn the routine exactly.
On his return the team that faced Hull City had been reconfigured. Moses wasn’t overly drilled, just told he would be playing right wing-back, that Conte had seen enough to know.

glosses: To cause to drill (practice); to train in military arts.

examples.text: The sergeant was up by 6:00 every morning, drilling his troops.
He [Frederic the Great] drilled his people, as he drilled his grenadiers.

glosses: To repeat an idea frequently in order to encourage someone to remember it.

examples.text: The instructor drilled into us the importance of reading the instructions.

glosses: To investigate or examine something in more detail or at a different level

examples.text: Drill deeper and you may find the underlying assumptions faulty.

glosses: To throw, run, hit or kick with a lot of power.

examples.text: He drilled down the court and made a three-pointer.
He drilled the ball to his teammate.

glosses: A tool or machine used to remove material so as to create a hole, typically by plunging a rotating cutting bit into a stationary workpiece.

examples.text: Wear safety glasses when operating an electric drill.

glosses: The portion of a drilling tool that drives the bit.

examples.text: Use a drill with a wire brush to remove any rust or buildup.

glosses: An activity done as an exercise or practice (especially a military exercise), particularly in preparation for some possible future event or occurrence.

examples.text: Regular fire drills can ensure that everyone knows how to exit safely in an emergency.

glosses: A short and highly repeatable sports training exercise designed to hone a particular skill that may be useful in competition.

examples.text: At today's practice, the football team performed a variety of goalkeeping drills.

glosses: Any of several molluscs, of the genus Urosalpinx and others, especially the oyster drill (Urosalpinx cinerea), that make holes in the shells of their prey.
